description: Common radiator node R of the thermal design (T3 line 6 with T4 and T5) against the ISS finite element panel mean temperature of the EATCS radiators, loops A and B, third orbit of the three FE cases. Values below are the inputs of the FE-002 entry of Thermal/test_report/build_test_report_cn.py; the test checks them against the FE model parameter table iss_fem/model/iss_spec.py, the FE results and the FE report.

fe.heat_input_definition: Qrad_L = feff_L mdot_L cp_nh3 (Tret_L - Tout_L), the enthalpy the NH3 of loop L gives up in its three radiator ORUs (iss_fem/model/iss_layout.py _loops); it feeds the 24 panels and the 24 NH3 nodes of the loop
fe.source: ISS FE model, COMSOL 6.3, report iss_fem/docs/REPORT.md sections 3.7 and 3.8 (BDF with manual 120 s steps from orbit noon to 16560 s, output every 120 s, event rows at the shadow boundaries) and chapter 5 (statistics over the last orbital period, the third orbit)

pointing.zero: sunlit: TRRJ zero pose, panel normal along the orbit normal, the Sun lies in the panel plane at every orbit angle when beta is 0 (edge to the Sun); shadow: front face to nadir
pointing.track: sunlit: roll about the station X axis (velocity, +XVV attitude) so that the Sun lies in the panel plane, normal = v x s / |v x s|; shadow: front face to nadir
pointing.source: FE report table 6 and section 3.5 (ATCS overview p16: edge to the Sun in daylight, face to Earth in the shadow); body +Z is the front normal, body -Z the back normal

orbit.source: FE orbit functions of summary.json (radius 6778137 m = 6378137 m + 400 km, inclination 0.90128803 rad, period 5553.6243 s, time from orbit noon), Sun direction sun_ecs with parallel rays and the cylindrical Earth shadow of radius 6378137 m (iss_spec ORBIT R_earth_m)

radiator.source: FE-002 inputs from the FE parameter table iss_spec.py: HRS geometry (3 ORUs per loop, 8 panels per ORU, width 3.4 m, wing from X -1.26 m to -23.25 m with 0.05 m gaps), MATERIALS hrs_pan (rho 3200 kg/m3, cp 900 J/kgK, t 2.5 mm, areal mass 8 kg/m2), PARAMS C_f (NH3 node 1 kJ/K per radiator panel, 22 tubes x 2.7 m of liquid NH3 plus tube wall) and cp_nh3 (4.61 kJ/kgK); the NH3 portion is entered in T5 as the liquid NH3 mass whose m cp equals 24 x C_f. Optics per case from OPTICS z93 and OPTICS_BY_CASE. The FE uses constant properties; the declared range covers the radiator temperatures of all runs of this case.

injection.source: FE-002 test configuration recorded per thermal design 9.4: the precondition of the case replaces q_SR + q_CR + q_BR + q_DR by the FE radiator heat input. The FE input enters through the D node: Q_D_W equals the FE input, C_D = 100 J/K (0.006 percent of C_R) and R_DR = 1e-4 K/W (equivalent total), so q_DR follows Q_D with a time constant of 0.01 s and T_D stays 1.4 K to 2.6 K above T_R. Controller01 and PDU01 here are this injection device, not ISS equipment.

auxiliary_nodes.note: S, J, C and B are not compared. Their explicit values only complete the six-node model; P_pv_W, P_load_W and Q_B_W are zero and SR, JC, CR and BR take 1e12 K/W, a very large resistance that represents no conduction, so they carry no heat to R.
auxiliary_nodes.source: FE-002 auxiliary nodes, not compared; explicit test values

solver.source: thermal design table 8: Radau is the implicit method for disparate thermal time scales (injection node 0.01 s against the radiator 13 min to 35 min); relative tolerance, temperature absolute tolerance and maximum step are scene settings; integration is split at the eclipse boundaries and at the FE heat-input samples (declared interpolation on continuous intervals); outputs are sampled on the accepted solution every 30 s and the statistics use a 5 s grid on the accepted solution

independent_reference.source: independent T4 with an Earth-centred quadrature and independent integration of T3 line 6 (fe002_support.py)

criteria.source: acceptance 5 K from the FE-002 entry; 0.1 percent heat input from the case instruction; the other tolerances are rounding or quadrature bounds of the independent references stated with each check; loop_difference_K bounds the linearization error of the hand estimate dT = dQ / (4 eps sigma 2A T^3), second order in dT/T: 1.5 dT^2 / T = 0.03 K for dT = 2.2 K at T = 220 K
